summary: Register an OAuth-capable app in your Salesforce org's Setup. As of Spring '26, Salesforce restricts creating new Connected Apps and now directs developers to External Client Apps instead — a change recent enough that general LLM knowledge misses it. No external review is required for use within your own org.
requirements: A Salesforce org with admin access to Setup (Developer Edition orgs are free)
A redirect URI (callback URL) for your app
The OAuth scopes your integration needs

steps.text: Log in to your Salesforce org and go to Setup.
In the Quick Find box, enter "App Manager", then open App Manager.
Click "New External Client App" (the current path — "New Connected App" is restricted as of Spring '26).
Fill in basic info: app name, API name, contact email.
Enable OAuth settings, set the callback URL, and select the OAuth scopes your app needs.
Save. Consumer Key and Consumer Secret are generated immediately — no external review for use within your own org.

blockers: As of Spring '26, new Connected Apps can no longer be created — use External Client Apps instead, or contact Salesforce Support if you specifically need a Connected App.
Distributing your app to other orgs (e.g. via AppExchange) is a separate, additional review process beyond the basic setup covered here.
Redirect URI must exactly match what's configured, or the OAuth flow fails.
Rate limits and API request allocations apply per org/edition.

AppExchange/public distribution review timelines were not researched for this guide; only basic in-org setup is covered.
verificationNotes: The automated pipeline's live run fetched only Salesforce developer-portal landing pages, correctly judged they didn't support any specific claims, and produced an empty guide rather than fabricate one — honest, but not useful on its own.

Manually browsed help.salesforce.com and developer.salesforce.com to fill the gap, and found something the automated pass (running on free models) would not have known: Salesforce restricted creation of new Connected Apps as of Spring '26 and now directs developers to External Client Apps — recent enough that it postdates most models' training data. This guide reflects the current (verified) path.
